{{pagebanner}}
'''Ella''' (also spelt 'Elle') is a beautiful small town in [[Uva]] province on the southern edge of [[Sri Lanka]]'s Hill Country. It is popular with tourists and makes a great base from which to explore the surrounding countryside.
[[File:SL Ella asv2020-01 img08 Little Adams Peak.jpg|thumb|300px|View of Little Adam's Peak]]
It's in the middle of beautiful countryside, with small vegetable plots in the valleys, tea plantations on the hill slopes and forests on the tops.

The climate throughout most of the year is typical of the high Hill Country, with a hot sun by midday, but a moderate air temperature. It will often rain in the afternoon, but only for an hour or so. A sweatshirt, or light jacket is needed at night. In December it can rain a lot! Heavy rain can cause tea harvesting to be suspended, dirt trails can turn to mud, and the emergence of leeches on greenery including along hiking paths and in tea plantations.

There's not much to do in Ella, and it gets quite busy with tourists, especially along the main street. The centre of town (predictably named Ella Rd) is a combination of shops, lots of small hotels and restaurants, and some bars. Instead of staying directly on the main drag, accommodation is much quieter just a street or two away from it.

Ella has a small post office and multiple banks with ATMs. Track bashers (rail enthusiasts) should particularly enjoy the line to [[Badulla]], where at the village of Demodara it does a 360-degree loop before crossing over itself.

==Get in==
[[File:Ella Railway Station Sri Lanka.jpg|thumb|Sign for Ella Railway Station]]

===By train===
'''Cyclone Ditwah'''

In November/December 2025, Cyclone Ditwah damaged 70% of the Sri Lankan railway network.
Repair work is ongoing (as of February 2026), but several lines are still out of service:
* Trains from Badulla and Ella travel as far as Nanu Oya (close to Nuwara Eliya) but don't continue to Kandy or Colombo.
* There are no trains from Colombo to Kandy, Matale, Ella or Badulla: These trains only travel as far as Rambukkana
* The lines are still open from Colombo to Galle/Beliatta, Chilaw, Trincomalee, Batticaloa and Jaffna.
Further information on [https://railway.gov.lk/web/index.php?option=com_content&view=article&id=917&lang=en Sri Lanka Railways' website] {{Dead link|date=November 2026 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}.

Ella is a few stops from Badulla at the end of the railway line that snakes through the Hill Country. Three day trains and one night train leave from Colombo via Kandy daily, taking 9-10 hours. Fares are cheap (2nd class Rs 900, 3rd class Rs 440 as of 2026) and the views are particularly spectacular. It's usually no problem getting a seat in 2nd/3rd class (seating is unreserved) going to Colombo or Kandy, as the trains from Badulla are quite empty until reaching Nanu Oya. However, getting a seat is challenging if travelling by train to Ella, as the train can be quite crowded until the last 2 or 3 hours of the journey. Ella's railway station is prettily quaint. 

Train seats are available for reservation 32 days in advance, but are all purchased immediately as soon as they become available. If you want a reserved seat, make arrangements for a local agency (such as [https://hopscotchtravels.com/how-to-book-the-ella-odyssey-train-updated-2026/ Hopscotch Travels]) to purchase the tickets as soon as they become available, or expect to pay several times the ticket price through a reseller. During high season, such as December-January, do not expect tickets to be available even from resellers in the last 1-2 weeks before the scheduled departure.

===By bus===
Buses go south through Ella Gap to Wellawaya where you can change for a number of destinations in the south of the island. There is also a direct bus service to Galle which stops at various locations along the south coast including Mirissa and Unawatuna.

When catching a bus from Wellawaya to Ella you need to catch a bus to Bandarawella - there are 2 routes, only one goes through Ella. There are tuktuk drivers who will try to take you to the wrong bus platform so that you take their tuk tuk.

The bus stops are at the southern end of Ella's main road, just south of Ella - Passara Rd. Buses to Ampara leave in front of the curd shop/Lavazza Barista shop.

Useful buses:
*8:45AM: Ella-Matara
*9:15AM: Ella-Ampara, via Monaragala (2 hr, Rs 184) and Siyambalanduwa. Onward buses to Pottuvil (for Arugam Bay) leaves from both destinations so no extra change in Wellawaya is required. A direct bus from Monaragala has a direct bus to Arugambay via Pottuvil (3½ hr, Rs 247).

==Get around==

{{mapframe|zoom=14|6.8666058|81.0569927}}

There are plenty of tuk-tuks around, but the best way to get around is to rent a scooter- most guest houses do this. Online carhire services exist such as [https://ceylontaxi.lk/ella-taxi-cab-service/ Ella Taxi Service].

==See==
* {{see|name=Little Adam's Peak|lat=6.8635341|long=81.0637794|image=SL Ella asv2020-01 img16 Little Adams Peak.jpg|content=A relatively easy hike to the east of the town center. Walk along the main road for 20 minutes to reach the path, cutting across tea plantations before the final climb up. Great views on Ella Rock and Rawana Falls. You can see the Newburgh Tea Estate on the other side (north). Busy during high season. There is a zip line near the bottom of the trail, available for a fee, though it won't save you time.}}
* {{see
| name=Nine Arch Bridge | alt= | url= | email=

| phone= | tollfree=
| hours= | price=Free
| wikidata=Q20722599
| lastedit=2024-08-13
| content=Famous beautiful rock bridge east of the town center. 45 minutes walk from the town center (Passara road, same as Little Adam's Peak and Newburgh Estate), then take a left to walk down to the bridge via a paved road and concrete stairs. Alternatively, walk along the train tracks from Ella railway station (but be careful to listen for approaching trains). If unsure, ask the locals, but not tuk tuk drivers, as they will want to take you along an expensive, circuitous route that will take you to near the bridge at track level. Can be a bit crowded with tourists, come early to enjoy the fresh air. Check the time tables to be able to see a train pass while you are there (but there will be around 4 trains passing between 10AM and 1PM). The bridge and Little Adam's Peak can be combined nicely, from the bridge it's another 5-km walk to the peak.
}}
* [[File:Rawana Falls.jpg|thumb|Rawana Falls]]{{see
| name=Ella Rock | alt= | url= | email=
| address= | lat=6.854722 | long=81.051944 | directions=
| phone= | tollfree=
| hours= | price=Rs 930 (for foreigners)
| wikidata=Q87194670
| lastedit=2024-08-13
| content=A more strenuous exercise than Little Adam's Peak. About 2 hours (each way) along the railway track (south of Ella) and through the tea plantations, for stunning views across the countryside. The first 1.5 km is along the railway track so keep an ear out for oncoming trains although they travel slowly. The locals who live near the bottom of Ella Rock have come up with the following idea: they obliterate existing tracks up the hill and create new ones every now and then. Tourists following guidebooks get completely lost, and suddenly, a local appears offering to guide them. Use an app that is based on Openstreetmap (Osmand, maps.me, komoot …) and follow the trails marked as ''Footpath to Ella Rock'' (or ''Footpath to Ella Rock (shortcut)'' for a shorter, but steeper track) and try to avoid walking to closely to the villagers' homes in order not to disturb them.
}}
* {{see|name=Rawana (Ravana) Falls|lat=6.8409997|long=81.0545064|image=SL Ella asv2020-01 img01 Ravana Falls.jpg|lastedit=2023-03-07|content=About 5 km away on the road south through Ella Gap. They're quite spectacular, especially during or after rainfall. Take your swimming costume for a refreshing dip, but beware of the touts selling tourist junk. You can catch frequent buses for about Rs 50, or better still walk (but catch a bus back up the hill). About half-way down the road you can stop off for a look at the small temple and a cave above it where, according to local legend, Sita was kept as a prisoner before being rescued by Rama. You are also quite likely to meet families of langur monkeys by the roadside.}}

==Buy==

==Eat==
[[File:Meal at Matey Hut, Ella, Sri Lanka.jpg|thumb|Four curries and a king coconut to wash it all down at Matey Hut]]
The home cooking in the guest houses and hotels is probably the best food in town. You can find a lot of tourist-oriented bars, cafes and restaurants on the main street.

{{Eat|name=Matey Hut|lat=6.87376|long=81.04631|directions=Near the railway overpass tunnel|phone=+94772583450|price=Rs 1000-1500 per person|lastedit=2025-04-03|content=Teriffic food! Quaint roadside stall with bench seating. Try the pumpkin curry and the green mango curry}}

* '''Down Town Rotti Hut''', right in the centre of town you can't miss it. Nice cold beers and good quality Kotthu Roti's. Recommend the beef!
* '''Rawana Holiday Resort''' is perched on a hill top with views down the valley, but you need to call ahead to book a dinner before 15:00. For Rs 400-500/person you will be served an explosion of flavors—about 8 small dishes with each order. 
* '''Ella Holiday Inn''' opened in 2005 at the Wellawaya Road junction in the centre of town is a good place for meals, snacks and drinks, sitting on the verandah looking out at life on the main street.
* '''Cafe Eden''' is on Ella - Passara Rd., near the start of the Nine Arch Bridge walking trail. It is ''the'' place to get lampreis in Ella.

==Drink==
Most of the cafes on the main street serve alcoholic drinks as well. You won't go thirsty in Ella!

===Budget===
There are a number of cheap guest houses scattered around town.

* '''Green Hill''', (wemalasooriya@yahoo.com) is on top of the Ella Gap overlooking green mountains with a nice view through the gap. The owners, Podi and Prasanna were very welcoming and provided authentic Sri Lankan meals including egg hoppers for breakfast. The rooms were constructed in the early 2010s and were of very good quality. It is a 200-m walk back to the centre of town and 1.5-km walk to Little Adam's Peak. The water was hot and the rooms were very modern and clean. Rs 2500/3000.

==Connect==

==Go next==
Take the train to [[Badulla]], [[Haputale]], [[Nuwara Eliya]] (Nanu Oya railway station) or [[Kandy]].

From the bus station on the main road, the following services are available (April 2025).

* [[Galle]] (4 departures per day, also stops at [[Mirissa]]) 
* [[Matara]] (7 departures per day)
* [[Ambillipitiya]] (2 departures per day)
* [[Thanamalwila]] (3 departures per day)
* [[Maligawila]] (3 departures per day)
* [[Kataragama|Katharagama]] (4 departures per day)
* [[Monaragala]] (3 departures per day)
* [[Ampara]] (4 departures per day)
* [[Kandy]] (3 departures per day, night buses only)
* [[Nuwara Eliya]] (5 departures per day)

Travellers bound for Yala National Park can board the bus to Matara or Galle and change busses at Pannegamuwa. Travellers headed to [[Arugam Bay]] can connect to a Pottuvil-bound bus in Monaragala.

==Stay healthy==

Don't walk in the countryside in shorts and sandals or flipflops, especially after it's been raining. There are lots of leeches that hang on to the vegetation by the side of tracks waiting for a nice juicy mammal to walk by. Take some Dettol or hand sanitizer with you and spray it on the offending leech, which will drop off.
